questions.q: How does this lesson define enterprise identity as a discipline?
options: Managing a person's digital identity once, centrally, with every system trusting that central source rather than maintaining an independent notion of who the person is
A Salesforce-specific feature with no application outside the Salesforce platform
A single password shared across every system in the company
A one-time project completed when a company first implements Salesforce
questions.explain: Enterprise identity is defined as centrally managing a person's identity once and having every connected system trust that central source, rather than each system independently managing its own notion of who the person is.

questions.q: When Salesforce acts as a SAML service provider (SP), which system actually authenticates the user?
options: Salesforce authenticates the user directly, with no external involvement
A corporate identity provider authenticates the user and sends Salesforce a SAML assertion that Salesforce verifies against its own configuration
The ERP system authenticates every Salesforce login
No authentication occurs when Salesforce acts as a service provider
questions.explain: As a SAML service provider, Salesforce trusts assertions posted by the corporate identity provider, verifying each one against its own configuration before granting access -- the IdP does most of the setup and the actual authentication work.

questions.q: What problem does Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning solve, per this lesson?
options: It solves encryption of data at rest
It automatically creates a Salesforce user account the first time someone signs in through a trusted identity provider, using attributes from the SAML assertion
It permanently deletes a user's Salesforce account the moment they leave the company
It replaces the need for any SSO configuration entirely
questions.explain: JIT provisioning solves the initial-account-creation problem -- automatically creating the Salesforce user record on first login using SAML assertion attributes, rather than requiring a user record to be pre-created manually.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Identity Connect and SCIM are used for, as distinct from JIT provisioning?
options: Encrypting Salesforce data at the field level
Ongoing synchronization -- keeping a user's Salesforce record current as their role, department, or employment status changes in the system of record, after initial account creation
Replacing SSO entirely so no identity provider is needed
Generating landscape diagrams automatically
questions.explain: Identity Connect (pushing updates from Active Directory) and SCIM (an open standard for the same purpose) handle ongoing synchronization after the initial JIT-provisioned account creation, keeping the Salesforce user record current as the employee's status changes.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect enterprise identity design to the security concerns introduced in Lesson 7?
options: It says identity and security are entirely unrelated topics
A gap in identity design, such as a stale account left active after a role change, is exactly the kind of enterprise-wide risk a well-designed identity landscape is meant to close off
It says Salesforce Shield fully solves all enterprise identity problems on its own
It says identity design only matters for companies with a single Salesforce org
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties identity design to enterprise security: a compromised identity provider or a stale access gap left over from a role change is exactly the enterprise-wide risk a well-designed identity landscape is meant to prevent.
